findings.message: This name is already declared in the same scope. The second declaration does not create a second binding, it overwrites what the name reaches, so every use of the name after this point gets whatever the last declaration bound and the earlier one becomes unreachable without ever being deleted. The two spellings that look intentional are the dangerous ones: a value and a type sharing a name compile fine and diverge later, and a second class silently replaces the first for every `new`, every `extends`, and every `instanceof` in the file. Rename one of them, or delete the declaration that is dead.
